hints.title: Symmetric Matrix Property
hints.text: In a valid word square, row k and column k must be identical strings, meaning the kth letter of every row forms the kth column.

hints.title: Prefix Map or Trie Lookup
hints.text: To select the kth row, all letters from row 0 to k minus 1 at column k establish the prefix that the kth word must start with.

hints.title: Backtracking with Prefix Filter
hints.text: Index words by all possible prefixes. Start with an empty square and try each word as row 0. At step k, compute the required prefix from previously chosen rows, fetch all candidate words with that prefix, append each candidate, and recurse.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
from collections import defaultdict
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def wordSquares(self, words: List[str]) -> List[List[str]]:
        n = len(words[0])
        prefix_map = defaultdict(list)
        for w in words:
            for i in range(n + 1):
                prefix_map[w[:i]].append(w)

        res = []
        curr = []

        def backtrack(step: int):
            if step == n:
                res.append(list(curr))
                return
            prefix = "".join(curr[i][step] for i in range(step))
            for candidate in prefix_map.get(prefix, []):
                curr.append(candidate)
                backtrack(step + 1)
                curr.pop()

        for w in words:
            curr.append(w)
            backtrack(1)
            curr.pop()

        return res
```

complexity.notes: Prefix dictionary allows constant-time candidate filtering per backtracking step.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing all permutations of words takes O(N^L) which is completely infeasible.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Prefix dictionary consumes O(N * L) space to prune search branches instantaneously.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Model column symmetry as prefix lookups for subsequent rows.
